_note: Starter catalogue from the playbook (3.2), extended freely. Place statuses and modern identifications are starting points: research verifies every one (3.4, 3.5) before it reaches a script. Text references are given only where they are standard; research adds the rest with the edition it cites. Western European, Finnic and Tibetan and Mongolian are added to the playbook's nine traditions so the balancing rule can place Dante, Milton, Goethe, Camoes, the Song of Roland, the Kalevala and Gesar.

lenses.name: Is it real
lenses.description: Does the evidence support the place the text names, and how strong is it?

lenses.name: Who claims it
lenses.description: Which community, state, temple or tourism body promotes the identification, since when, and why.

lenses.name: What is there today
lenses.description: What physically stands at the site now, who visits, and who looks after it.

lenses.name: What it means in the argument
lenses.description: Why the text puts this place at this point: what the setting does for the idea.

lenses.name: How retellings changed it
lenses.description: How later versions, translations, films or regional tellings moved or reshaped the place.

lenses.name: Money and politics on it today
lenses.description: Heritage listings, pilgrimage economies, development projects and political claims that sit on the site.

epics.title: Iliad

geography_status.note: The wanderings have been mapped onto the Mediterranean since antiquity; almost every stop has rival claimants.
